title: CareVision
summary: Multimodal clinical AI workflow integrating Gemini 2.0 Flash with explainability-first human review gates and offline-capable fallback.
problem: Assisted review requires dependable, explainable workflows with explicit confidence gates rather than opaque generative outputs.
solution: A multimodal PWA combining Gemini 2.0 Flash structured outputs, step-level audit logging, PostgreSQL persistence, and offline-capable inference fallback.
architecture: Case-study context: Assisted review across multimodal inputs needs a clear boundary between model output and human judgment. The interface therefore emphasizes structured responses, auditability, and bounded fallback behavior.
Client workflow: A typed React PWA presents the review flow and keeps state transitions visible to the operator. Components: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix UI, Zustand.
Inference boundary: FastAPI coordinates structured multimodal inference and preserves a review-oriented response contract. Components: FastAPI, Gemini 2.0 Flash.

Persistence and continuity: PostgreSQL and SQLAlchemy support durable records while the offline-capable path keeps the workflow useful when connectivity is limited. Components: PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy.
The README describes a React 18 and TypeScript progressive web application using Vite, Tailwind, Radix UI, and Zustand.
FastAPI coordinates structured multimodal inference through Gemini 2.0 Flash; the portfolio frames output for human review.
PostgreSQL and SQLAlchemy support persistent records; the portfolio case study describes audit logging and an offline-capable fallback.
outcomes: Gemma hackathon submission with multimodal inputs, audit logging, and offline fallback.
Presented the system as decision support, never as diagnosis or treatment.
Kept audit logging and fallback behavior visible as part of the product story.
